strengths: The paper offers an elegant and principled conceptual framework by viewing attention through the lens of Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT) regularized by an arbitrary prior distribution via KL divergence, rather than treating positional encodings as ad-hoc heuristics.

The engineering implementation of GOAT is clever and practical: by partitioning the head dimension into content and positional subspaces and using an unscaled vector concatenation trick, the additive prior is realized entirely within standard, unmodified SDPA/FlashAttention kernels without materializing dense $L \times L$ attention bias matrices.

The theoretical analysis in Appendix F is rigorous and insightful, deriving a classification theorem showing that bounded, translation-equivariant, SDPA-compatible relative priors must belong to the finite trigonometric polynomial family, as well as formalizing the connection between ALiBi-style recency and maximum-entropy distributions.

The explanation of attention sinks as optimal transport defaults under low-signal queries is compelling, providing a clean method to decouple structural defaults (sinks) from semantic representation vectors.

The empirical validation spans diverse domains—synthetic copy/retrieval tasks, language modeling length extrapolation, DNA sequence modeling, and zero-shot resolution extrapolation in Vision Transformers—demonstrating the broad applicability of the method.
weaknesses: The scale of the language modeling experiments is relatively modest (125M parameters trained on 4B tokens). While sufficient as a proof-of-concept, demonstrating that these properties and in-distribution perplexity advantages persist at larger scales (e.g., 1B+ parameters, larger token budgets) would substantially strengthen the empirical claims.

The baseline comparisons for length extrapolation are mostly limited to standard RoPE, ALiBi, and basic Position Interpolation (PI), omitting more competitive modern RoPE extensions (such as YaRN, LongRoPE, or recent learnable attention-bias methods like CoPE).

In Figure 4(b), the reported 36% peak CUDA memory reduction for GOAT relative to RoPE is surprising given that both methods nominally execute through FlashAttention; the exact source of this memory difference (e.g., unfused RoPE operations vs. fused SDPA) warrants a clearer explanation.

Subspace allocation requires reducing the effective content dimension $d_c = d_h - d_p$. The manuscript would benefit from a more comprehensive ablation on the sensitivity of model performance to the choice of $d_p$ and the computational overhead of computing the positional vectors and the sink MLP during training and generation.

strengths: Principled theoretical formulation: Deriving attention with priors from Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT) by generalizing Shannon entropy regularization to KL divergence provides a clean, unified view connecting relative positional encodings, ALiBi recency biases, and attention sinks.

Hardware-friendly implementation: The algebraic factorization of trigonometric relative terms and rank-one sink biases into dedicated query/key subspaces allows seamless integration into standard FlashAttention / SDPA kernels without materializing dense $L \times L$ attention bias matrices.

Theoretical characterization (Appendix F): Theorem 2 nicely proves that SDPA compatibility, translation equivariance, and boundedness mathematically restrict the admissible relative prior family to finite trigonometric polynomials.

Broad empirical validation: The method is tested across multiple modalities and benchmarks, including 125M LM pre-training and 16x length extrapolation on C4, Passkey / NIAH retrieval, DNA sequence modeling, and zero-shot resolution extrapolation on ImageNet-1k ViT.
weaknesses: Evaluation scale: Experiments are conducted predominantly at the 125M parameter scale trained on 4B tokens. Demonstrating scalability on larger models (e.g., 1B+ parameters) or longer pre-training budgets would strengthen the empirical claims for LLM deployment.

Comparison with advanced long-context techniques: While baselines include standard RoPE, ALiBi, and basic Positional Interpolation (PI), comparisons against modern RoPE variants (e.g., YaRN, LongRoPE) or recent contextual positional approaches (e.g., CoPE) are missing.

Head dimension trade-off: Reserving $d_p$ dimensions out of $d_h$ (e.g., $d_p = 12$ out of $d_h = 64$) reduces the effective subspace available for semantic content representations ($d_c = d_h - d_p$). An ablation analyzing the sensitivity to $d_p$ and the impact of reduced semantic capacity on downstream semantic benchmarks would be valuable.

Clarification on memory benchmarks: In Figure 4(b), GOAT reports a 36% reduction in peak CUDA memory compared to RoPE (1.83 GB vs. 2.86 GB). Since both operate via fused SDPA/FlashAttention, the source of this substantial memory overhead in the RoPE baseline needs clearer explanation.

strengths: Principled Theoretical Formulation: Grounding self-attention in Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT) with an arbitrary prior distribution provides a clean, unified foundation for additive positional biases and attention sinks. Theorem 5.1 and the sensitivity bounds (Theorem 5.4) offer an insightful mathematical justification for why low-signal queries collapse to defaults and how prior-driven sinks decouple structural defaults from semantic key norms.

Hardware-Friendly Implementation: Injecting additive Fourier relative priors and key biases directly into standard, unmodified Scaled Dot-Product Attention (SDPA) and FlashAttention via subspace factorization (Eqs. 20–24) is an exceptionally neat algebraic contribution. It avoids materializing dense $L \times L$ bias matrices while circumventing custom kernel engineering.

Rigorous Theoretical Justification for the Parameterization: Appendix F presents non-trivial classification results (Theorem 2), proving that under SDPA-compatibility, translation equivariance, and boundedness, the relative prior family collapses precisely to finite trigonometric polynomials, while ALiBi-style recency emerges from a maximum-entropy principle (Theorem 3).

Multi-Domain Empirical Validation: The method is validated across diverse domains, including synthetic copy-mixture tasks, causal language modeling length extrapolation (up to $16\times$), long-context retrieval (Passkey and Needle-in-a-Haystack), human genomic modeling, and zero-shot resolution extrapolation in Vision Transformers on ImageNet.
weaknesses: Scale of Language Model Evaluations: The main causal language modeling experiments are conducted on 125M parameter models trained on 4B tokens of C4. While sufficient for proof-of-concept, modern positional encoding and long-context evaluations typically benchmark at larger parameter scales (e.g., 1B–7B) and larger token budgets to verify whether the extrapolation benefits and perplexity gains persist without degradation at scale.

Omission of Standard Downstream Benchmarks: The NLP evaluation relies primarily on perplexity curves, synthetic passkey retrieval, and Needle-in-a-Haystack tasks. Standard downstream language understanding and reasoning benchmarks (e.g., MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag, GSM8K) are omitted, leaving open whether reserving head dimensions for prior features affects general downstream task capabilities.

Capacity Trade-Off of the Content Subspace: Reserving $d_p = 2R + 2$ dimensions from the total head dimension $d_h$ reduces the available capacity for semantic content dot-products ($d_c = d_h - d_p$). In standard architectures with $d_h = 64$, reserving 12 to 32 dimensions constitutes a significant reduction in content representation space. The paper lacks an ablation study examining how varying $d_p$ and frequency rank $R$ affects representation quality on semantics-heavy tasks.

Missing Comparisons with Modern Long-Context Techniques: While compared against standard baselines (RoPE, ALiBi, and Position Interpolation), the manuscript does not compare against more recent long-context extrapolation and learnable bias methods such as YaRN, CoPE (Contextual Position Encoding), or FIRE.

strengths: Principled and elegant theoretical foundation: Reframing scaled dot-product attention through one-sided Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT) provides a clean mathematical justification for additive structural priors and gives a first-principles account of attention sinks as optimal transport defaults in low-signal regimes.

Hardware- and kernel-friendly implementation: By factorizing queries and keys into content and positional subspaces and using an exact norm-scaling trick (Equations 23–27), GOAT integrates seamlessly into standard FlashAttention/SDPA kernels without materializing $O(L^2)$ attention bias matrices.

Rigorous characterization results: Appendix G provides compelling theoretical theorems showing that finite-dimensional SDPA-compatibility and translation equivariance force bounded priors to be finite trigonometric polynomials (Theorem 2), that ALiBi-style recency is the unique maximum-entropy prior under a mean-lag constraint (Theorem 3), and that sinks correspond to minimal rank-one key biases (Theorem 4).

Comprehensive empirical evaluation across diverse domains: The method is validated not only on standard language modeling (125M on C4, 1.23B on FineWeb) and long-context retrieval (Passkey, Needle-in-a-Haystack), but also on genomics (hg38 DNA modeling) and 2D vision (zero-shot resolution extrapolation on ImageNet-1k).
weaknesses: Content subspace capacity trade-off: By reserving $d_p = 2R + 2$ dimensions out of each head dimension $d_h$ for the prior (e.g., $d_p = 10$ or $18$ when $d_h = 64$), the effective content dimension $d_c$ is reduced. The paper does not systematically explore whether this content capacity trade-off becomes a bottleneck in highly semantic-dense tasks or when using smaller head dimensions.

Scale of language model training: The 1.23B FineWeb model was trained on only $\approx 3.13\times 10^9$ tokens (Table 8), which is significantly undertrained relative to standard compute-optimal (Chinchilla) or modern production baselines. Demonstrating that the in-distribution parity and extrapolation gains hold at full compute convergence would strengthen the claim.

Evaluation on downstream LLM tasks: The language modeling evaluation is limited to validation perplexity and synthetic retrieval tasks (Passkey / NIAH). Benchmarking on standard downstream evaluation suites (e.g., MMLU, ARC, HellaSwag) would help ensure that dedicating head dimensions to structural priors does not harm general downstream capabilities.

strengths: Principled Theoretical Framework: Framing self-attention through the lens of one-sided Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT) with non-uniform priors offers a clean and conceptually satisfying perspective. It provides a first-principles mathematical rationale for additive position biases and formalizes attention sinks as optimal defaults in low-signal regimes.

Hardware-Friendly Kernel Compatibility: The vector factorization and scaling trick (Equations 23–27) allows an arbitrary additive Fourier log-prior and key-only broadcast sink to be evaluated inside an unmodified Scaled Dot-Product Attention (SDPA) call. This avoids materializing $L \times L$ bias matrices and maintains compatibility with IO-aware kernels like FlashAttention.

Rigorous Theoretical Characterization: Appendix G provides valuable theoretical justifications, including a classification theorem showing that bounded, translation-equivariant, SDPA-compatible relative priors are necessarily finite trigonometric polynomials, as well as an information-theoretic derivation of ALiBi-style recency as a maximum-entropy distribution.

Broad Empirical Validation: The method is validated across a wide variety of domains and modalities, including synthetic long-context retrieval (Passkey and Needle-in-a-Haystack), 125M and 1.23B language modeling with extensive extrapolation (up to $16\times$), genomic sequence modeling, and 2D image resolution extrapolation on ImageNet-1k.
weaknesses: Head Dimension Overhead and Capacity Trade-off: Reserving a positional subspace $d_p = 2R + 2$ inside each attention head reduces the effective semantic content dimension $d_c = d_h - d_p$. For typical head dimensions ($d_h = 64$ or $128$), devoting 10 to 32 dimensions to position represents a non-trivial capacity reduction (up to 25%), which may become a bottleneck in capacity-constrained setups.

Comparisons with Modern Long-Context Techniques: The language modeling length extrapolation experiments primarily compare against vanilla RoPE and ALiBi. In modern LLM literature, length extrapolation typically utilizes specialized frequency scaling techniques (e.g., YaRN, NTK-aware scaling, or LongRoPE). While position interpolation (PI) is included in the synthetic retrieval benchmarks, including advanced RoPE scaling baselines in the language modeling evaluation would make the empirical comparison more comprehensive.

Unclear Profiling Details for Memory Savings in DNA Modeling: Figure 4(b) reports a 36% reduction in peak CUDA memory allocation for GOAT compared to RoPE (1.83 GB vs. 2.86 GB) under identical batch sizes and context lengths. The source of this substantial memory difference is not sufficiently detailed in the text (e.g., whether RoPE suffered from intermediate rotary tensor materialization or lack of kernel fusion compared to GOAT).

Pretraining Budget Scale: The 1.23B parameter model on FineWeb is trained on ~3.13B tokens, which is undertrained relative to standard compute-optimal training regimes. While the downstream extrapolation trends are clear, confirming the stability of the learned Fourier parameters and sink margins over tens or hundreds of billions of tokens would further reinforce the findings.

strengths: Unifying Theoretical Framework: Framing self-attention through one-sided Entropic Optimal Transport (EOT) provides an elegant, principled justification for why standard attention corresponds to a flat uniform prior, and naturally derives additive log-priors as the optimal solution under non-uniform structural priors.

First-Principles Analysis of Attention Sinks: The paper offers a rigorous information-theoretic explanation for attention sinks (Theorem 5.1 and Theorem 5.4), demonstrating that they naturally arise as defaults in low-signal regimes and formalizing why prior-based sinks decouple structural bias from content representation norms.

Hardware-Efficient Design: Rather than materializing expensive L x L relative bias matrices, GOAT factorizes the prior into positional Fourier features and key biases embedded directly into query-key dot products via an algebraic scaling trick, maintaining full out-of-the-box compatibility with optimized kernels like FlashAttention.

Broad and Multimodal Evaluation: The empirical evaluation is thorough and covers multiple domains and scales, including 125M and 1.23B language modeling (demonstrating smooth length extrapolation up to 16k context where RoPE fails), synthetic retrieval (Passkey and NIAH), DNA sequence modeling, and zero-shot resolution extrapolation in Vision Transformers.
weaknesses: Content Capacity Trade-Off: Reserving a subspace of size d_p = 2R + 2 from the head dimension reduces the effective content dimension d_c = d_h - d_p. Although the paper shows good overall perplexity, a more systematic investigation of whether this capacity reduction affects high-capacity dense semantic benchmarks or reasoning tasks would strengthen the submission.

Evaluation on Downstream Long-Context Tasks: For the 1.23B model, long-context evaluation is primarily assessed via language modeling perplexity and synthetic Needle-In-A-Haystack tasks. Evaluating real-world long-context tasks (such as LongBench, SCROLLS, or long-document summarization/QA) would provide stronger evidence of practical utility.

Contrast with Fourier/Kernel Relative Position Encodings: Parameterizing relative attention biases with trigonometric/Fourier representations has antecedents in kernel methods and relative position encodings (e.g., Choromanski et al., 2024). While the EOT framing and exact SDPA factorization are distinctive, the main text could benefit from a clearer discussion delineating the functional differences from prior Fourier-based relative attention schemes.
